question.text:
What is the output of the following code?

#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    int x = 2, y = 0;

    switch (x) {
        case 1:
            y = y + 1;
        case 2:
            y = y + 2;
        case 3:
            y = y + 3;
            break;
        default:
            y = y + 4;
    }

    printf("%d", y);
    return 0;
}

question.text:
What is the output of the following code?

#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    int i, j, sum = 0;

    for (i = 1; i <= 4; i++) {
        for (j = 1; j <= 4; j++) {
            if (j == i)
                continue;

            if (i + j > 5)
                break;

            sum = sum + i + j;
        }
    }

    printf("%d", sum);
    return 0;
}

question.text:
What is the output of the following code?

#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    int a = 1, b = 2, c = 3;

    if (a++ > 1 && ++b > 2 || c++ == 3)
        printf("%d %d %d", a, b, c);
    else
        printf("%d %d %d", c, b, a);

    return 0;
}
  1. $\texttt{2\ 3\ 4}$
     
  2. $\texttt{2\ 2\ 4}$
     
  3. $\texttt{4\ 2\ 2}$
     
  4. $\texttt{1\ 2\ 3}$

question.text:
What is the output of the following code?

#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    int x = 3, y = 4, z;

    z = x++ + ++y;

    printf("%d %d %d", x, y, z);
    return 0;
}
  1. $\texttt{4\ 5\ 8}$
     
  2. $\texttt{3\ 5\ 8}$
     
  3. $\texttt{4\ 4\ 7}$
     
  4. $\texttt{4\ 5\ 9}$

What is the output of the following code?

#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    int i, j, count = 0;

    for (i = 1; i <= 3; i++) {
        for (j = 1; j <= i; j++) {
            count = count + j;
        }
    }

    printf("%d", count);
    return 0;
}
